topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestChallengerRespondsToMultipleInvalidClaims`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed by Claude on behalf of @ajsutton.

## Test
`TestChallengerRespondsToMultipleInvalidClaims` in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/challenger_test.go`

## Failure
- **Job:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/124471/workflows/e3b91150-4f58-413a-8936-5d0c34f81f59/jobs/4986655/tests
- **Branch / commit:** `aj/refactor/remove-super-cannon-from-challenger` @ `8f4cace5e26b258135807449e8bd892a7df3a4f3`
- **Duration:** 47.5s (failed); subsequent retry passed → flake confirmed
- **Error site:** `op-devstack/dsl/proofs/dispute_game_factory.go:449` → `DisputeGameFactory.Create(...)` call reverted

## Error
```
assertions.go:387:
  Error Trace: op-devstack/dsl/contract/call.go:73
               op-devstack/dsl/proofs/dispute_game_factory.go:449
               op-devstack/dsl/proofs/dispute_game_factory.go:240
               op-devstack/dsl/proofs/dispute_game_factory.go:222
               op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/challenger_test.go:50
  Error:       Received unexpected error:
               upstream dep 0 (*plan.Lazy[*types.Transaction]) failed: upstream dep 2 (*plan.Lazy[TxData]) failed:
               upstream dep 7 (*plan.Lazy[uint64]) failed:
               execution reverted: 0x014f6fe561012191321bdd79be321cf0c9e6e881964206564290a08224b73118dfc597e2
```

The selector `0x014f6fe5` is the `Create` revert reason; the trailing 32 bytes appear to be a hash payload from the custom error.

## Notes
- Test calls `dgf.StartSuperCannonKonaGame(attacker)` which deploys a new dispute game via the factory. The factory `Create` call reverted ~47s into the run.
- Same test on the same PR passed on retry, so this is a flake — not a regression from the PR.
- A flake-fixer agent is investigating root cause.

topIssues.title: geth: rapid disk use after State Snapshot Generation
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
[Check this Explore](https://optimistic.grafana.net/goto/IGUHd7JNg?orgId=1)

Sometimes when a state snapshot is generated, it causes a sudden rapid disk usage that far exceeds normal usage.

This doesn't happen for all generations, but happens sometimes on base nodes.

## Debugging

The snapshot comes from Rebuild: https://github.com/axelKingsley/go-ethereum/blob/b2b0e1da8cac279bf0466885d1abdc5d93402f41/core/state/snapshot/snapshot.go#L717, 
based on the logs.

I added "[Failed to load snapshot" to my search](https://optimistic.grafana.net/goto/MxHlOnJHg?orgId=1), and found that every time we do this snapshot generation is due to a failure to load the snapshot, because it doesn't match the head:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e9ab0cc-2ba6-462d-a253-df2c8d337c4f)

What I notice is that the `have` is being updated to the `want`, but then the `want` changes. Not yet sure why that is. Perhaps there's a secondary process or application that's messing with the snapshot?

topPRs.title: op-supernode: serve full superroot RPC from durable state post-activation
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Stacked on top of #20558. Adds the infrastructure needed for `superroot_atTimestamp` to serve **`Data`, `OptimisticAtTimestamp`, and `CurrentL1` entirely from durable verifier state** post-interop-activation, so `CurrentL1 ≥ game.L1Head` is sufficient for op-challenger to know it is only acting on cross-safe-consistent data.

Three commits:

1. **Serve `OptimisticAtTimestamp` from durable verified records** + per-chain L1 inclusion in `VerifiedRecord` and `DenyRecord`. Denylist overlay preserves the original optimistic block when a chain was invalidated and replaced.
2. **Preinterop / pre-activation live fallback** for `Data` (the existing `chain.VerifiedAt` path), so preinterop fault-proof acceptance tests can still observe `Data != nil`.
3. **Durable per-chain observation snapshot** so in-flight (post-activation, pre-commit) timestamps can serve `OptimisticAtTimestamp` partial views without a live SafeDB read. This closes the rewind race and is what makes the durability guarantee complete.

## Design overview

### `VerifiedRecord` (already in #20558, extended here)
- Per-chain `ChainObservation` (L2 head, L1 head, OutputV0 preimage). Aggregate `L1Inclusion` and per-chain output roots are derived on demand.
- `DenyRecord` and `InvalidHead` carry per-chain `L1Inclusion` captured at decision time.

### `ObservationsSnapshot` (new)
- Single `(timestamp, map[chainID]ChainObservation)` value, replaced atomically by the verifier each round in `checkChainsReady`.
- Replacement (including dropping chains that previously had a block but no longer do) is what closes the rewind race.
- `checkChainsReady` now returns partial results plus an `allReady` bool. NotFound from a chain is no longer fatal — the round is treated as Wait, but the partial snapshot is still persisted so the challenger can serve per-chain partial visibility (needed to identify which chain's optimistic step is the InvalidTransition boundary).
- Cleared on rewind in `applyRewindPlan` so post-rewind queries cannot return stale observations.

### Verifier frontier `CurrentL1`
- `Interop.VerifierCurrentL1()` exposes the durable frontier (already maintained in `frontier_bucket`/`current_l1`). The handler prefers it over the live aggregate.
- Advances every Wait round (`refreshCurrentL1OnWait`) so it tracks live L1 within a few blocks even between L2 batches.

### Live reads
The handler now consults live state **only** when `verifierActiveAt(timestamp) == false` — i.e. there is no provider configured (preinterop build) or the timestamp is pre-activation. Post-activation, every cross-safe-derived field is durable.

## Live vs durable audit

### Pre-interop activation (`!verifierActiveAt(timestamp)`)

Live reads only — there is no cross-safe state to be durable.

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| `Data` | live `chain.VerifiedAt` + `chain.OutputRootAtL2BlockNumber` per chain |
| `OptimisticAtTimestamp` | live `chain.OptimisticOutputAtTimestamp` (with chain-side denylist overlay) + `chain.OptimisticAt` per chain |
| `CurrentL1` | `aggregate.CurrentL1` (live `chain.SyncStatus().CurrentL1`, reduced by registered verifiers' L1s) |
| `CurrentSafeTimestamp`, `CurrentLocalSafeTimestamp`, `CurrentFinalizedTimestamp` | live, from `chain.SyncStatus()` |
| `ChainIDs` | sorted keys of the chains map |

This branch handles preinterop deployments and any pre-activation timestamp on an interop deployment. The challenger's `CurrentL1 ≥ game.L1Head` guarantee doesn't apply here because the verifier isn't producing it; preinterop fault games don't depend on cross-safe verification anyway.

### Post-interop activation (`verifierActiveAt(timestamp) == true`)

No live reads of cross-safe data.

| Field | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Data` | `Interop.StoredSuperRootAtTimestamp` → `VerifiedRecord.ResponseData()` | Returns nil if no record. No live fallback. |
| `OptimisticAtTimestamp` | `Interop.StoredOptimisticAtTimestamp` → `VerifiedRecord.Chains` if present, else `ObservationsSnapshot.Chains` if it covers the timestamp; both paths apply the denylist overlay | Returns empty (and partial within the snapshot) when the verifier hasn't observed the timestamp at all. No live fallback. |
| `CurrentL1` | `Interop.VerifierCurrentL1()` (durable verifier frontier in bbolt's `frontier_bucket`/`current_l1` key) | Falls back to live aggregate only before the verifier has populated the frontier (true cold start, pre-activation). |
| `CurrentSafeTimestamp`, `CurrentLocalSafeTimestamp`, `CurrentFinalizedTimestamp` | live `chain.SyncStatus()` | Local node sync state, not cross-safe data. Not consumed by the challenger for game decisions. |
| `ChainIDs` | sorted keys of the chains map | Matches the dependency set. |

### How each durable source is built

`VerifiedRecord` (committed by `applyPendingTransition` on `DecisionAdvance`):
- Per-chain L2 head, L1 head, OutputV0 preimage all snapshotted at observation time inside `buildVerifiedRecord` (using the `result.L1Heads` populated by `verifyInteropMessages` from `obs.L1Heads`).
- Aggregate `L1Inclusion()` is `max(per-chain L1Head)`, derived not stored.

`ObservationsSnapshot` (replaced by `observeRound` each round in `observationsDB.Set`):
- Built in `checkChainsReady` from per-chain `OptimisticAt(ts)` + `OutputV0AtBlockNumber(...)` calls. Each chain that returns successfully gets a `ChainObservation`; chains that return NotFound are absent.
- Replaced atomically in a single bbolt transaction so RPC reads see a consistent (timestamp, chains) view, not a torn snapshot.
- Cleared on rewind (`applyRewindPlan`) so a later round at a now-rewound timestamp cannot serve stale observations.

`DenyList` overlay (applied to both sources by `optimisticFromObservations`):
- Per-chain `LastDeniedAtHeight(L2Head.Number)` returns the original (denied) preimage and per-chain L1 inclusion captured at decision time. Overrides the verified/observed entry when present so the response surfaces the originally-observed (now-replaced) block, matching the semantic the challenger relies on.

### Why `CurrentL1 ≥ game.L1Head` is now sufficient

For any post-activation timestamp T:

1. The handler reads `verifiedProvider.VerifierCurrentL1()` — the durable frontier the verifier has fully digested. No live data influences `CurrentL1`.
2. If a `VerifiedRecord` exists at T → cross-safe view, all chains, full preimages and per-chain L1 inclusions. `VerifiedRequiredL1 ≤ CurrentL1` by construction (the verifier sets `CurrentL1 = parent(L1Inclusion)` on commit).
3. If no record at T but the observation snapshot covers T → partial cross-safe-candidate view. Each entry's `RequiredL1` is the per-chain L1 head observed in that round. Chains absent from the snapshot are absent from the response, exactly the per-chain partial visibility the challenger needs.
4. If neither covers T → empty response. The verifier hasn't observed T, so any answer would be a guess. The challenger correctly treats this as InvalidTransition.

In all three cases the response is built from a single bbolt-consistent snapshot. Chain rewinds between when the round committed and when the RPC fires can't desync `CurrentL1` from the per-chain entries, because both come from the same durable store.

### Live reads after activation

The only post-activation live reads are the L2 timestamp aggregates (`SafeTimestamp`, `LocalSafeTimestamp`, `FinalizedTimestamp`) — local node sync metadata that doesn't feed challenger decisions. Everything derived from L1 ≤ CurrentL1 — `Data`, `OptimisticAtTimestamp`, `CurrentL1`, denylist overlays — is durable, deterministic, and consistent.

## Tests

- `op-supernode/...` unit tests: pass.
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial/...` (11 tests): pass.
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs-singlechain/...`: pass.
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/isthmus/preinterop/...` (8 tests): pass.
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/isthmus/preinterop-singlechain/...`: pass.

topPRs.title: test(contracts): stage past NUT bundles in L2 fork upgrades
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Stages committed prior NUT bundles during live L2 fork upgrade test setup so fork tests can run on chains that have not yet applied earlier NUT-backed forks.

Failure shape this fixes:

```
ExecuteNUTBundle: Transaction failed - Deploy StorageSetter Implementation - Proxy: implementation not initialized
```

That happens when the current bundle expects Karst-era `ConditionalDeployer` / L2CM infrastructure that is not present on the forked chain.

This adds:
- Ordered NUT bundle discovery from `op-core/nuts/fork_lock.toml` via a new `scripts/go-ffi/go-ffi nut-bundles` command.
- Reusable `ExecuteNUTBundle.executePath(string)` and `ExecuteNUTBundle.executeAll(NetworkUpgradeTxn[])` APIs; `execute()` is preserved as a thin wrapper around the current bundle path.
- Test-only `PastNUTBundles` library that fetches ordered prior bundles, extracts each bundle's L2CM from the final `IL2ProxyAdmin.upgradePredeploys` call, and stages or skips each bundle via a centralized skip policy.
- `foundry.toml` read permission for `../../op-core/nuts/`.
- Wiring into `L2ForkUpgrade_TestInit.setUp()` only, after `generateScript.run()` and before common state capture.

**Skip policy**

Same-L2CM skipping alone is too broad: Karst and a future Interop bundle can share the same final L2CM, so a naive same-L2CM skip drops Karst even when the forked chain has never applied it. `_shouldSkipPriorBundle` applies these rules in order:
- Karst direct CREATE2 bootstrap supersession: skip when the current bundle already contains a byte-identical `(to, data)` transaction whose `to == Preinstalls.DeterministicDeploymentProxy`. These direct CREATE2 calls are not idempotent; staging Karst first would cause a CREATE2 collision in the current bundle.
- Karst state-aware staging: when Karst's L2CM matches the current bundle, still stage Karst if the live fork's `ConditionalDeployer` is uninitialized.
- Generic same-L2CM skip for non-Karst bundles.

This is intentionally a named-rules list, not residual per-transaction de-dup. Executing only a prior bundle's "unique tail" can violate bundle ordering and prerequisites.

**Non-goals**

- No production activation changes.
- No genesis fork staging — `L2GenesisForkUpgrade.t.sol` is intentionally untouched.
- No Interop wrapper replay (`setFeature(INTEROP)`, `ETHLiquidity` funding, optional `CrossL2Inbox` deploy/upgrade). The FFI is fork-name-aware so wrapper dispatch can be added later without redesigning discovery.

**Tests**

Added coverage for:
- Ordered NUT bundle FFI behavior, lock parsing, path resolution, error cases.
- `ExecuteNUTBundle.executePath` / `executeAll` happy path and revert-message preservation.
- L2CM extraction and rejection of malformed final txs (wrong target / wrong selector / wrong calldata length / non-zero high padding / zero address / empty bundle).
- Same-L2CM skip, Karst direct CREATE2 bootstrap skip, Karst same-L2CM staging when `ConditionalDeployer` is not initialized, and non-overlapping different-L2CM execution.

**Forward-compat check**

Verified against a PR #20397-shaped branch (Karst + Interop lock entries, current bundle is Interop-shaped, both committed bundles decode to the same final L2CM):

```
PastNUTBundles: 2 prior bundle entry/entries discovered
PastNUTBundles: staging fork=karst ...
PastNUTBundles: skipping fork=interop ... (L2CM matches current)
```

Full `test/L2/fork/L2ForkUpgrade.t.sol` passed on that branch. This validates ordered discovery, Karst prerequisite staging, and same-L2CM Interop skip. It does not validate Interop wrapper replay, which remains out of scope.

**Metadata**

- Fixes #20524

topPRs.title: feat(op-node): serve superroot_atTimestamp for non-interop chains
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a new \`superroot\` JSON-RPC namespace on op-node with a single method \`AtTimestamp(timestamp)\`, mirroring op-supernode's wire contract exactly so existing dispute infrastructure (op-challenger, op-dispute-mon) can point \`--supernode-rpc\` at op-node URLs on non-interop chains.

Closes #20552 (server side; consumer-side wiring & acceptance tests are follow-up scope per the original plan).

## Why

After the super-roots upgrade, fault dispute games for non-interop chains will reason over super roots rather than output roots. op-challenger and op-dispute-mon already consume \`superroot_atTimestamp\`, but today only op-supernode serves it — and non-interop chains don't run op-supernode. Per @ajsutton on the issue: *"This is critical since we need to move to super dispute games before interop activates."*

## What

Two commits:

1. **\`refactor(safedb): extract L1AtSafeHead into shared helper\`** — pure refactor, no behavior change.
   - Move the L1-at-safe-head walkback algorithm from \`op-supernode/.../virtual_node.go\` into \`op-node/node/safedb/l1_at_safe_head.go\` so op-node and op-supernode share one implementation.
   - op-supernode delegates; existing \`ErrL1AtSafeHeadNotFound\` / \`ErrL1AtSafeHeadUnavailable\` are re-exported from the new package.
   - Algorithm-level tests relocate to the new package (10 sub-cases). Virtual-node-specific delegate checks stay where they are.

2. **\`feat(op-node): serve superroot_atTimestamp for non-interop chains\`** — the feature.
   - New \`op-node/node/superroot_api.go\`. Single chain → single \`ChainID\` in response.
   - Registered as \`superroot\` namespace in \`registerAPIs\` (always-on; harmless on chains that haven't activated super-root games).
   - Field semantics documented in code and matched against op-supernode's \`Aggregate\` helper:
     - \`CurrentSafeTimestamp\` ← \`SafeL2.Time\`, \`CurrentLocalSafeTimestamp\` ← \`LocalSafeL2.Time\`, \`CurrentFinalizedTimestamp\` ← \`FinalizedL2.Time\`.
     - \`VerifiedRequiredL1\` (and verified-branch \`OptimisticAtTimestamp[chainID].RequiredL1\`) come from \`safedb.L1AtSafeHead\` — correctness-critical because op-challenger gates \`InvalidTransition\` on this value.
     - Optimistic-only branch (block beyond LocalSafeL2 but within UnsafeL2) uses \`L1Origin\` as \`RequiredL1\`, matching op-supernode.
     - Pre-genesis / beyond-UnsafeL2 / safeDB-not-found degrade to \`Data: nil\` with sync fields populated. Errors only on transport failures.
   - No activation gate (per @ajsutton's issue resolution): identical pre- and post-Interop.

## Out of scope

Per the original plan, follow-up work (separate PRs):
- Devstack wiring (\`op-devstack/sysgo/l2_challenger.go\`, \`dsl.NewSupernodeFromQueryAPI\` adapter).
- New \`preinterop-superroots\` acceptance gate exercising op-challenger + op-dispute-mon end-to-end against op-node.
- Cross-implementation parity test driving both op-node and op-supernode from the same fixture.
- README updates.
- op-proposer CLI flag (\`--super-node-rpcs\`) — config field exists but no flag is wired today; tracked separately.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go test ./op-node/node/safedb/...\` — 10 algorithm sub-cases pass.
- [x] \`go test ./op-node/node/...\` — 9 superroot API cases + existing op-node tests pass.
- [x] \`go test ./op-supernode/...\` — virtual_node delegate tests pass; superroot/chain_container/engine_controller suites unchanged.
- [x] \`go vet ./op-node/... ./op-supernode/...\` — clean.
- [x] \`just lint-go\` — clean (zero issues).
- [ ] Acceptance / e2e (follow-up PR).

## Notes for reviewers

- **No deletions in op-node.** Phase 0's only deletion is the body of \`simpleVirtualNode.L1AtSafeHead\` in op-supernode (now a one-line delegate).
- **Wire surface is minimal.** Only \`superroot_atTimestamp\` is registered. The interface-conformance check uses a test-only adapter rather than a method on the live struct, which would otherwise leak \`superroot_superRootAtTimestamp\` as an extra wire method.
- **Fallback path is intentional.** When \`safeDB.L1AtSafeHead\` returns \`ErrL1AtSafeHeadNotFound\` (e.g., snap-sync gap, or target beyond latest), op-node degrades to optimistic-only with \`Data: nil\` — matching op-supernode's \`notFound\` branch (chain_container.go → superroot.go). Consumers (op-challenger trace provider, op-dispute-mon enricher) already treat \`Data: nil\` as "not yet verified."

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
